text_masked: On April 26, 2003, avid mountaineer PERSON goes hiking at Utah's Canyonlands National Park without telling anyone. He befriends lost hikers PERSON and PERSON and gives them directions. While guiding them, he shows them an underground pool. The three have fun, and that afternoon, the girls invite him to a party that is being held the following night. PERSON expresses half-hearted interest and says goodbye to the girls, who head home. He continues through a slot canyon in Bluejohn Canyon. While climbing, an boulder from which he is hanging comes loose and causes both to fall, which traps his right arm against the wall. PERSON attempts to move the boulder, but it does not budge; he also soon realizes he is alone. He shortly begins recording a video diary using his camcorder to maintain morale as he chips away parts of the boulder with a pocket knife. At one point, the knife falls from his hand, and he is forced to use his bare feet and a little branch to recover it. Over the next five days, PERSON rations his food and remaining 300ml of water, of which he accidentally spills a portion. He struggles to keep warm at night, and is forced to drink his urine when his water runs out. Every morning, he enjoys a brief period of sunlight when the canyon is not in shadow. He also sets up a pulley using his climbing rope in a futile attempt to lift the boulder. Determining that chipping away at the boulder will only make it settle further, he attempts to amputate his arm, but finds that his dull blade can only make shallow cuts. The tool's other implements prove more effective, but are unable to cut through his bones. Throughout the days, PERSON becomes desperate and depressed and begins hallucinating about escape, relationships, and past experiences, including his family and his former girlfriend, PERSON. He also imagines going to the party he was invited to and having fun. During one hallucination, PERSON realizes his mistake was that he did not tell anyone where he was going or for how long. PERSON has a vision of his future son on the sixth day, spurring his will to survive. PERSON fashions a tourniquet from CamelBak tube insulation and uses a carabiner to tighten it. Then, using his knowledge of torque, he breaks the bones in his arm and, using the multi-tool, slowly amputates it. PERSON then wraps the stump to prevent exsanguination and takes a picture of the boulder before rappelling down a rockface. He then finds some rainwater collected while descending down, drinks the stagnant water due to dehydration, and continues. He spots a family on a hike in the desert and calls for help. They give him water and alert the authorities; a Utah Highway Patrol helicopter brings him to a hospital. Years later, PERSON gets married and has a son. He also continues climbing and always leaves a note telling his family where he has gone.

In an underground barracks, they discover a tripwire set by the Germans, which is promptly triggered by a rat; the explosion almost kills PERSON, but PERSON saves him, and the two escape. They arrive at an abandoned farmhouse, where a German plane crashed after being shot down in a dogfight with Allied aircraft. PERSON and PERSON save the burned pilot from the wreck and attempt to help him. Despite this, the pilot fatally stabs PERSON in the abdomen before PERSON shoots the pilot dead. PERSON comforts PERSON as he dies from blood loss, promising to complete the mission and to write to PERSON's mother. PERSON's rings and dog tag, as well as PERSON's letter, he is picked up by a passing British unit who have noticed the smoke from the burning plane. A destroyed canal bridge near Écoust-Saint-Mein prevents the British lorries from crossing, and PERSON chooses to part with them. He uses what is left of the bridge to cross alone, and comes under fire from a sniper. Exchanging shots, PERSON confronts the sniper in his tower perch, whereupon he and the sniper shoot each other simultaneously; the sniper is killed, while PERSON is struck in the helmet and knocked unconscious. Encountering the platoon, PERSON strangles one and escapes pursuit by jumping into a river. He is swept over a waterfall before reaching the riverbank. There, she is greeted by the White Rabbit, a Dormouse, a Dodo, Talking Flowers, and identical twins Tweedledum and Tweedledee, who all apparently know her. PERSON asserts that she is dreaming, but learns from Absolem the Caterpillar that she is destined to slay the Jabberwocky and end the tyranny of the Red Queen. The group is ambushed by the ravenous PERSON and the Red Queen's knights, led by the Knave of Hearts. All are captured except PERSON, who escapes, and the Dormouse, who takes one of the PERSON's eyes. The Knave informs the Red Queen of PERSON's return, and is ordered to find her immediately. The Cheshire Cat guides PERSON to the Mad PERSON, March Hare, and Dormouse's tea party. The Red Knights and the Knave of Hearts disrupt the party, but PERSON manages to hide in a teapot. The PERSON then takes her to a safe place. He explains that the Red Queen took over Underland, usurping her sister, the White Queen. While in the woods, the Red Knights find the two, but the PERSON gives himself up so that PERSON can escape. She is found by the Knave's Bloodhound, named Bayard, who is allied with the resistance. He takes PERSON to the Red Queen's castle, where she becomes a giantess again after eating another PERSON. Infiltrating the palace as a courtier named "Um", PERSON learns that the vorpal sword, the only weapon capable of killing the Jabberwocky, is locked inside the PERSON's den. The Knave makes a pass at PERSON, which she rebuffs, but the jealous Red Queen orders her beheading. PERSON obtains the sword and returns the PERSON's eye. He gratefully helps her escape the castle and delivers her to the White Queen, who gives PERSON a potion that returns her to her normal size. The Cheshire Cat uses his shapeshifting powers to free the Mad PERSON, who incites rebellion amongst the Red Queen's subjects. Just before his chrysalis closes, he advises her to fight the Jabberwocky, save Underland, and stop the Red Queen for good. The Queens gather their armies on a chessboard-like battlefield and send PERSON and the Jabberwocky to decide the battle in single combat. PERSON says farewell to her friends, then wishes to return home. PERSON awakens in the rabbit hole. text_masked: A man narrates a letter addressing people he will miss. In the Indian Ocean eight days earlier, the man wakes to find water flooding his boat. It has collided with a wayward shipping container, ripping a hole in the hull. The man uses a sea anchor to dislodge the container, then changes tack to raise the hole out of the water. He patches the hole and uses a manual bilge pump to remove the water from the cabin. The boat's navigational and communications systems have been damaged by saltwater intrusion. The man tries to repair the marine radio and connects it to one of the boat's batteries. When he climbs the mast to repair an antenna lead, he sees an oncoming tropical storm. When the storm arrives, the man runs before the wind. He intends to heave to, but as he crawls to the bow to hoist the storm jib, he is thrown overboard and regains the deck only after a desperate struggle. The boat capsizes and rights itself; during a second roll, which throws the man overboard again, the boat is dis-masted and most of the equipment is destroyed. After going below deck and being knocked out by colliding with a post, he regains consciousness to find the boat sinking, so he abandons ship in an inflatable life raft. When the storm has passed, he salvages whatever he can from his sinking boat and transfers it to the raft. Before the boat sinks, he tends to the gash on his forehead. As the man learns to operate a sextant, he discovers he is being pulled towards a major shipping lane by ocean currents. He survives another storm, but his supplies dwindle and he learns too late that his drinking water has been contaminated with sea water. He improvises a solar still from his water container, a plastic bag, and an aluminum can, producing fresh water, and he snags a fish, but it is snapped up by a shark before he can reel it in. The man's raft is passed by two container ships, but it is unseen despite his using signal flares. He drifts out of the shipping lane with no food or water. On the eighth day, he writes a letter, puts it in a jar, and throws it into the ocean as a message in a bottle. Later that night, he sees a light in the distance. He uses pages from his journal along with charts to create a signal fire. The fire grows out of control and consumes his raft. Falling into the water, he loses hope and attempts to drown himself. text_masked: About 20 years before the story takes place, solar flares irradiate the Earth, killing over 99% of the world's population. The survivors gather in a network of safe cities and build primitive humanoid robots, called Pilgrims, to help rebuild and operate in the harsh environment. These robots have two unchangeable protocols: They cannot harm any form of life and may not repair, modify, or alter themselves or other robots in any way. Initially seen as humankind's salvation, they are relegated to manual labor when they fail to stop the advance of desertification. Society has regressed due to the lack of technology besides the Pilgrims, as a lack of functional aircraft or other transport prevents travel and cars are a rare commodity, putting humanity on the brink of extinction. In 2044, PERSON—an insurance investigator for ROC, the company that manufactures Pilgrims—investigates a report from PERSON, a police officer who shot a robot he claims was modifying itself. As PERSON looks for a robot they suspect was stealing parts, it leads him outside the city. When he finds it inside a shipping container, it sets itself on fire. As he and a team open up the burned robot to see what it was hiding, they discover the robot had a rare nuclear battery that could power a robot indefinitely. They are able to power up the robot once more, but when he asks it why it set itself on fire, it burns out again. PERSON salvages the remains and speculates to PERSON, his boss and brother-in-law, that there may be a "clocksmith", someone who illegally modifies robots, who is overriding the second protocol. Incredulous, PERSON rejects this possibility, but offers PERSON a transfer out of the city if he can find evidence. PERSON had asked for the transfer to a city on the coast, because he feared raising his unborn child in the decaying city, even though PERSON is skeptical whether the ocean still exists. PERSON's pregnant wife, PERSON, initially rejects his plans, but she eventually relents. PERSON and PERSON investigate a brothel, where they find PERSON, a modified robot that PERSON subsequently shoots in the leg. When PERSON objects, PERSON says that PERSON's owner will lead them to the clocksmith; PERSON also threatens to kill PERSON if he does not split the proceeds of the battery on the black market. PERSON follows PERSON's owner to a clocksmith named Dr. PERSON, who claims not to know who altered PERSON, an action that would destroy PERSON's CPU. PERSON leaves the burned robot's CPU with her and offers to give her the battery if she can locate information on the clocksmith. When PERSON installs the modified CPU in PERSON, PERSON begins self-repairing. PERSON contacts PERSON, who alerts PERSON; however, ROC intercepts PERSON's message and sends a team of assassins to PERSON's laboratory. PERSON is killed, but PERSON escapes in a car driven by PERSON. When PERSON takes them into a maze of stanchions, both cars crash; the assassins are killed, and PERSON is injured. PERSON takes PERSON with her into the desert, where they are joined by three other robots, none of whom will obey PERSON's orders. However, the first protocol forces them to prevent his death. Desperate to return to the city to be with his pregnant wife, PERSON makes contact with PERSON, who sends PERSON to recover him. PERSON threatens PERSON's life and destroys two of the robots, who have objected to his actions; PERSON kills PERSON with a flare gun before he can also destroy PERSON. PERSON's partner flees after taking a battery from one of the robots. PERSON's boss discloses that the predecessor to the first PERSON was a quantum mind created with no security protocols and no artificial restraints on its computational power. Before they deactivated it, its makers tasked it with designing the security protocols that govern Pilgrims. PERSON's boss informs PERSON that no one has been able to break PERSON security protocols, because they were created by the unrestricted quantum mind and ROC purposefully limited the computational power of all subsequent AI. ROC forces PERSON to accompany a team sent to kill PERSON and the unknown clocksmith before the robots can evolve further beyond human understanding. When PERSON objects to their kidnapping PERSON's wife and baby daughter, PERSON, the leader, shoots him and leaves him for dead. Meanwhile, PERSON meets the robot responsible for modifying the others. The robot says that he and the other robots plan to go to the radioactive area where humans cannot go. Initially skeptical, PERSON eventually accepts that the robot naturally evolved, like humanity. The robot cannot understand why PERSON is afraid of dying, as death is a normal part of human living, just as the impending extinction of humanity is normal. "No lifeform can inhabit the planet eternally." It points out that the androids were conceived of and built by humans, so humanity will continue to exist through the robots that they created. Accepting this, PERSON gives them his battery, which they use to complete a new design, a sort of dog/insect robot. The robots repair a vehicle for PERSON, and he leaves for the city. When PERSON reaches the robot outpost, he destroys two of the four robots. PERSON finds the dying PERSON and returns to the outpost as PERSON wounds PERSON and kills the evolved robot. PERSON kills all ROC assassins except for PERSON, though he is further wounded in the battle. As PERSON prepares to kill PERSON, the new robot saves his life by pushing PERSON off a cliff in violation of the first protocol. PERSON fears the uninhibited robot will now attack him and prepares to shoot it, only to lower his weapon as his wife arrives with their child. He works the crane so PERSON and the new robot can cross to the other side of the canyon into the irradiated area. PERSON and his wife take a car and drive toward the city on the coast. PERSON appears to be dying of his injuries, but takes comfort in their child. As she drives PERSON suddenly breaks out into a smile and tells PERSON she can see the ocean ahead.

A nuclear plant in Hong Kong goes into meltdown when a hacker causes the coolant pumps to overheat and explode. Soon after, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange is hacked, causing soy futures to rise. The Chinese government and FBI determine that the hack was performed using a remote access tool. Captain PERSON of the People's Liberation Army cyberwarfare unit is tasked with finding the hacker and enlists the aid of his sister PERSON, a networking engineer. He meets with FBI Special Agent PERSON in Los Angeles and reveals core parts of the code in the tool was written by himself and PERSON, his college roommate, during their time at MIT. PERSON requests that PERSON, who is in prison for hacking banks, be offered a temporary release in exchange for his services. PERSON, knowing how necessary he is to the investigation, demands new terms: his prison sentence commuted if his assistance leads to the hacker's identification and capture. He is required to wear an ankle bracelet monitor and be accompanied by deputy U.S. Marshal PERSON. PERSON manipulates the update system on PERSON's phone GPS that tracks his location, allowing him to follow his own lead and arrange a meeting with the hacker's partner at a restaurant. While they wait, he tells PERSON about his past, but the partner does not arrive. PERSON discovers a camera watching them and, following it to the connected computer, messages the hacker that he is now on his trail. Clues uncovered by PERSON and PERSON lead the team to Hong Kong, where they work with Police Inspector PERSON. The team traces the stock trade money to a paramilitary operative named PERSON. PERSON, PERSON, PERSON, and PERSON, along with a Special Duties Unit team, raid PERSON's hideout, and a shootout ensues in a drainage tunnel, resulting in the deaths of PERSON and several officers as PERSON and his men escape. The nuclear plant has stabilized enough to have a data drive recovered from the control room, but it is corrupted by radiation. The National Security Agency's Black Widow software has the ability to repair the data, but they refuse to allow the Chinese access. Reluctantly sanctioned by PERSON, PERSON hacks into the NSA and uses Black Widow, discovering that the hacker's server is based in Jakarta. PERSON finds out the hacker has been buying high-resolution satellite photos of a site near Seri Manjung, Malaysia. For his illegal hack, the NSA and FBI demand PERSON's return to prison. PERSON's superiors advise him to turn PERSON over to the U.S. government, but he instead alerts PERSON to their plans. Meanwhile, one of PERSON's men secretly plants a tracking device on PERSON's car. As PERSON and PERSON, who have become romantically involved, argue about his fleeing alone, PERSON is blown up by a rocket launched by PERSON; PERSON and PERSON, arriving on the scene, manage to shoot several of PERSON's men before they are both killed. PERSON and PERSON escape on a subway train, and she uses her connections to charter a plane to Malaysia. PERSON deduces that the hacker's attack at the nuclear plant was merely a test for a later plan: to sabotage a large dam and destroy several major tin mines in Malaysia, allowing the hacker to make a profit buying tin options. In Jakarta, he hacks into a bank's computer and transfers the hacker's funds into PERSON's Swiss bank account, then forcing the hacker, PERSON, to contact him. PERSON and PERSON agree to meet and discuss a partnership; PERSON anticipates a double-cross and arms himself with makeshift weapons and body armor which he conceals under his clothes. Though PERSON insists PERSON and PERSON come alone, they bring their henchmen. PERSON spots them and alerts PERSON, who orders them to a new location in a park during a large religious procession. PERSON trails them but is caught at gunpoint by PERSON. As he is being frisked, PERSON blindsides and stabs PERSON to death with a sharpened screwdriver. PERSON's men catch up and a firefight ensues; PERSON is shot several times but manages to kill the reinforcements. PERSON stabs PERSON with a knife before PERSON kills him. He reunites with PERSON, who treats his wounds, before they leave Indonesia.

K learns of her romantic ties with former blade runner PERSON. CEO PERSON wants the secret to replicant reproduction to expand interstellar colonization. He sends his replicant enforcer, PERSON, to monitor K. An unidentified figure engages several prostitutes in the city, including one named PERSON, to keep eyes on K. At PERSON's farm, K finds the date 6.10.21 carved into the tree trunk and recognizes it from a childhood memory of a wooden toy horse. Because replicant memories are artificial, K's holographic AI girlfriend Joi suggests that this is evidence that K was born, not created. K discovers in LAPD records that two children born on that date have identical DNA, but are inexplicably registered as being opposite genders, and that the girl died from a genetic disorder. K's search for the boy leads him to an orphanage, but the records from the year in question are missing. K recognizes the orphanage from his memories and finds the toy horse in the furnace where he remembers hiding it. He then visits replicant-memory-maker Dr. PERSON, who confirms that his memory of the orphanage is a real memory that someone lived, leading K to conclude he is the deceased replicant woman's son. K then fails a baseline test, marking him as rogue. When he implies to PERSON that he killed the replicant child, she gives him 48 hours to pass the test, or he will be retired himself. Joi hires prostitute replicant PERSON to sync with to be able to have sex with K. The following morning, PERSON places a tracker in K's jacket prior to leaving. K then takes the wooden toy horse to be analyzed for its origin, which leads him to the ruins of a now radioactive Las Vegas. There he finds PERSON, who informs him that the deceased replicant woman was named PERSON, and that he is the father of PERSON's child. PERSON had helped the Replicant Freedom Movement scramble the birth records to protect the child's identity. PERSON then left the child with the Movement to ensure the hunted child would not be found through him. PERSON, who has killed PERSON, tracks K to Las Vegas. She kidnaps PERSON, destroys Joi, and leaves an injured K behind. Using PERSON's tracker, the Movement rescues K. Their leader, PERSON, reveals that PERSON's child was actually a girl. Fearing that PERSON may give up the freedom movement to PERSON and endanger the child, PERSON urges K to kill him. K deduces that the memory of the toy horse actually belongs to Dr. PERSON, who is PERSON's daughter. PERSON takes PERSON to meet PERSON, who offers PERSON a duplicate PERSON in exchange for information about the child's whereabouts. PERSON refuses the offer, so PERSON has PERSON kill the duplicate. As PERSON transports PERSON to be tortured off-world, K intercedes. He fights and drowns PERSON but is mortally wounded in the process. K tells PERSON that he will be presumed dead, and is now free to go to his daughter, and then takes him to Dr. PERSON's facility. Standing outside the facility, he hands PERSON the toy horse. PERSON enters the building and meets Dr. PERSON, while K dies on the front steps.

Katia is approached at a subway station by a man calling himself PERSON. He tells her that 47 is on his way to kill her, and offers her protection, while hinting that he has information about the man she's seeking. 47 finds and attacks the pair, who are able to escape, but not before 47 grazes Katia's arm with a sniper bullet. PERSON and Katia hide out in a hotel room. He explains that he is an operative for a corporation known as Syndicate International and that the man she's seeking is her father. Katia shows him the clues she has put together and asks PERSON to tell her everything he knows about her father. Based on the languages he knows, his age, his love of orchids and medical condition (lung cancer), Katia deduces where her father must be living. Before she can tell PERSON, 47 enters, leaving PERSON for dead and capturing Katia. Once Katia awakens, 47 explains to her that she is an Agent, designed by her father to be better than even 47. He explains that her name "Katia van Dees" is a homophone for her real name, "Quatre-vingt-dix"; which is French for "90". He shows her how to use her heightened senses in combat and the two fight against Syndicate forces. They are confronted by PERSON, who is revealed to have surgically implanted subdermal titanium body armor, making him impervious to gunshots. After fighting off PERSON, 47 and Katia manage to escape. Katia makes 47 promise that he won't harm her father and finally reveals PERSON's location — Singapore. Elsewhere, 47's handler PERSON, learning of his situation, contacts another Agent with a contract in Singapore. 47 and Katia track down PERSON, who apologizes to Katia for abandoning her, saying that he only wanted to keep her safe and referring to 47 as her "brother". Just then, Syndicate soldiers attack the group and they are forced to flee. During the escape, PERSON is captured by the Syndicate, but not before 47 slips him an explosive-rigged inhaler. PERSON tortures PERSON under the supervision of Syndicate director PERSON, but PERSON refuses to reopen the Agent program. 47 hacks into the Syndicate announcing system and Katia crashes a stolen helicopter into the building; 47 disguises himself as a firefighter to get inside undetected. The two fight their way through Syndicate security forces, and 47 is once again confronted by PERSON. 47 defeats him by electrocuting him. On the rooftop, 47 and Katia mop up the rest of the Syndicate's troops, but not before PERSON escapes in a helicopter with PERSON. In mid-air, PERSON detonates the inhaler, killing himself and the director. 47 then calls PERSON and confirms his first target (PERSON) has been eliminated. When PERSON asks about the second target (implied to be Katia), 47 drops his phone off the side of the building. As the two prepare to leave, they are confronted by Agent 48, an exact look-alike of Agent 47, who tells them "PERSON says 'Hello'" before he, Agent 47, and Katia fire. PERSON discovers a rescue dog tangled in rope and frees it, naming it Sherlock and feeding it his sausage. He then finds an ambulance parked outside and tries to call for help using the radio, but only receives an automated announcement. PERSON searches for a spare battery, but has no luck. He does find a generator in a flooded basement room, but it is ruined from immersion and almost electrocutes him. He is barely in time to charge the battery again. Despite being awake for over 36 hours, running low on food, and having cut his hand from cranking the generator, he continues to come up with clever ways to charge the battery (e.g. using his foot and later a rod). Looters break into the hospital and steal food, drugs and saline water needed for the baby. One comes in PERSON's room and tries to steal food, but gets run off by Sherlock. PERSON, a U.S. Air Force fighter pilot, volunteers to be a part of an experiment on 14 test subjects that forces human bodies to adapt to the super-cold methane liquids and the ultra-low oxygen atmosphere of Titan. He is joined by his wife PERSON, a medical researcher, and their son PERSON, at the Titan I research area. The initial results are promising. PERSON becomes able to swim at incredible speeds and stay underwater for 42 minutes. Meanwhile, PERSON befriends and comforts PERSON, the wife of another volunteer, PERSON. PERSON's training becomes increasingly intense as he and the others adapt to increasingly Titan-like environments. PERSON finds that some of his hair is falling out, and one of the team members starts convulsing and dies. PERSON notices the veins of all the test subjects becoming darker. Fellow volunteer PERSON has a mental breakdown which causes him to attack his wife, PERSON. PERSON takes a break by sitting at the bottom of their swimming pool, where large amounts of his skin are shed. PERSON's concern grows, and she begins experimentation on a sample of his blood, finding that it is indeed becoming darker. PERSON undergoes corneal surgery to accommodate the low light on Titan. When he later has complications, PERSON confronts PERSON about PERSON's changes, but he divulges nothing. PERSON suffers another mental breakdown and throws PERSON through a window, killing her instantly. He is shot and killed by military police. While visiting PERSON in the medical facility, PERSON steals his key card and sneaks into PERSON's office. She finds reports of autopsies of the numerous deceased test subjects, discovering that they were having their DNA infused with animal DNA in an attempt to create the next human species, Homo titaniens. During a meeting with NASA, PERSON is chastised for doing forced evolutionary experimentation without proper evidence or ethical reasons, and is threatened with having his operation shut down. PERSON confronts him on the same issue, and he admits to her and PERSON that he does not actually know what the surviving subjects will eventually become. PERSON willingly undergoes major surgery to adapt to his new senses and become fully ready for Titan. He and Tally, the only other surviving test subject, complete their training and finish their transformations into Homo titaniens. PERSON is horrified when the significantly-transformed PERSON loses the ability to talk, now communicating in a low frequency that is undetectable by normal human ears. Tally kills her husband, later visiting PERSON at his home. PERSON and PERSON hide while military police surround Tally and PERSON. Tally kills a member of the police before she is killed, and then PERSON easily kills many more. When PERSON and PERSON confront him, PERSON flees, realizing what he has become. The military hunt for PERSON, but it is PERSON who finds him on a hill they often jog to. The military arrives and arrests them. PERSON wakes to find PERSON in critical condition, due to his newly evolved incompatibility with Earth's atmosphere. PERSON is forced to give him a chemical solution that acts similarly to a lobotomy, erasing all of his memories. However, she actually gives him a harmless saline solution instead, allowing him to escape. PERSON begins killing soldiers as PERSON and PERSON flee with Dr. PERSON, an assistant to PERSON who disagrees with his methods. The group find a heavily wounded PERSON, giving him first aid. PERSON arrives but his men disobey an order to fire upon unarmed PERSON, PERSON and Dr. PERSON. The colonel, who has been vocally against PERSON's experiments, soon arrests PERSON for his treachery. PERSON and Dr. PERSON become researchers at the Titan II facility, using more ethical methods than PERSON had. PERSON is shown exploring Titan, flying under his own power over a methane lake.

PERSON brings her in for questioning and accidentally coughs up blood into her face. He has her released and is hospitalized, though he soon checks himself out against medical advice. The billboards have further strained PERSON's relationship with her son, PERSON, and she recalls that her last interaction with PERSON was an argument (during which she lashed back by saying "hope you get raped"). Her abusive former police officer ex-husband PERSON confronts her about the billboards and ends up revealing that, shortly before PERSON's murder, he had turned her down when she asked to come and live with him. Later, at his mother's suggestion, PERSON arrests PERSON's friend PERSON on trivial drug possession charges to put pressure on PERSON. Knowing his death is imminent following the hospitalization, PERSON spends an idyllic day with his wife, PERSON, and their two daughters, then commits suicide later that night to spare his family from watching him die slowly. A distraught PERSON reacts to the news by assaulting PERSON and throwing him out of a second-storey window. This is witnessed by Abercrombie, PERSON's replacement, who fires PERSON. Before his death, PERSON wrote several letters, including one to PERSON. PERSON delivers it, interrupting an unknown man who was menacing PERSON at work. After the billboards are destroyed by arson, PERSON retaliates by tossing Molotov cocktails at the police station. PERSON, an acquaintance of PERSON, happens to pass by and extinguishes PERSON's burning clothes before providing PERSON with an alibi. He notes the number on the man's Idaho license plate and then scratches the man's face to get a DNA sample, passively accepting the resulting beating. PERSON and PERSON fight, so PERSON sleeps on the couch. Later that night, they are visited by Mr. B.'s colleague, Dr. PERSON, who is looking for Mr. B. When PERSON and PERSON can't keep their stories straight about Mr. B., PERSON levels a gun at them and forces them to confess. Mr. B. had mailed PERSON a photo that covers the next night, but it was taken before his death, meaning that the machine can be set to take photos more than 24 hours in advance. The photo shows blood on the window, Mr. B.'s hat on the friends' couch (PERSON has taken to wearing the dead man's hat), and a picture of a green coil resembling the broken device on the ground next to Mr. B.'s corpse. PERSON theorizes that "time" did not kill Mr. B. for trying to change the future; rather, he knocked over a coil in his storage unit and the released gas killed him. PERSON talks with PERSON to try to devise a way to prevent events, but PERSON knocks him out and locks him in Mr. B.'s storage unit; he does not believe PERSON's theory and intends to prevent a paradox, making sure that events correspond to the photo happen no matter what. Trying to find a way out of the locked storage unit, PERSON searches PERSON's purse and finds the photo with the blood, Mr. B.'s hat, and the painting of the coil; he realizes that he must be able to escape in order to paint the coil the next day, so that Mr. B. could take a picture of it in the first place. Finding Mr. B.'s keys, PERSON escapes, goes to the machine, and calls PERSON, threatening to destroy it if PERSON does not stop. A fight ensues, culminating with PERSON smashing PERSON's head in. When making the painting to match PERSON's photo, PERSON realizes a discrepancy. He discovers that the camera also takes a photo at 8 am, a truth which PERSON kept to herself. PERSON reveals that she has been using the morning photos to send herself messages to manipulate events, and rekindle her relationship with PERSON. The sex photo is one of those missing from Mr. PERSON's wall, from a drunken night (recalled as charades night by PERSON) a month ago (the other missing photos are ones of PERSON and PERSON being affectionate, which she took down from the wall when she first discovered the machine). The intruders are the Wilsons' doppelgängers: Red (PERSON's doppelganger, who she met all those years ago), Pluto (PERSON's pyromaniac, facially scarred double), PERSON (PERSON's sadistic double) and PERSON (PERSON's animalistic double). Red is the only double who can speak, albeit in a raspy voice. She explains that they are called "the Tethered", as they share a soul with their counterparts and have come to "untether" themselves. The Wilsons are separated and terrorized by their doppelgängers. PERSON discovers that Pluto mirrors his actions. After PERSON kills PERSON, the family escapes. They watch the news and learn that the Tethered have been murdering their equivalents across the city then joining hands to form a human chain (similar to the one from the Hands Across America demonstration) that surrounds the city. Arriving at the boardwalk, the Wilsons find many townspeople slaughtered. The road is blocked by a burning car. PERSON, realizing it is a trap set by Pluto, orders everyone out of the car.
